items.name: Child's shackle
items.description: A shackle too small for any grown wrist, stamped with the Bureau's mark.

items.name: Mourner's cap
items.description: A black-gilled toadstool from the banks of Gloom Creek, where the drowned graves are. Wenna swears by it.

items.name: Carrion boar tallow
items.description: Rendered fat, rank as the cliffs it came from. It burns long and yellow.

items.name: Khaven's goods
items.description: Candles, a bolt of wool, a family's pewter: taken from Khaven as 'toll'.

items.name: Charnel silk
items.description: A skein of grey spider-silk from the Carrion Heights, strong as cord and cold to hold. Dorra Vey says it takes a dye like nothing else.

items.name: Harl Emmet's noose
items.description: A length of tarred hemp, grey with grave-mud, still tied in a Khaven knot: three turns and a tuck.

items.name: The picket's order-roll
items.description: Oiled sheets rolled tight in a leather tube, every one sealed with a sun on a bar of sand.

items.name: The Reckoner's slate
items.description: A pane of cold, pale glass scratched from edge to edge with names, a number after each. It is heavier at one end, as if the sum were.

items.name: Bundle of tallow candles
items.description: A dozen of Cato Brisk's candles wrapped in sacking and tied with twine. Rank as a boar, and they burn all night.

documents.title: Forty Sovereigns
documents.text:
A notched tally-stick, with a scrap of paper wound round it in a clumsy hand:

Bureau wagon, Oakhaven run.
Two, small, taken on at Khaven gate. Sound.
Forty sovereigns: twenty paid at the gate, twenty at the toll.
Ride them north by the Peaks road. Hand on at the gate to the Concord escort.
No questions, as agreed.
documents.canonStatus: GAME-ONLY: the handover, the price and the route. Sandthrone working for the Concord follows world_bible.md.

documents.title: The Low Row
documents.text:
From the sexton's register of Khaven, the low row by the creek:

Tamsin Ade, drowned in the spring. Laid with salt on her tongue, as is proper.
Old Pell, the fever. Salt, and a coin for the road he's on now.
The Fenwick twins, both in the one box. Salt.
Harl Emmet, the gallows. No salt. The Sandthrone would not allow it.

(Added later, in a shaking hand:) The creek came up in the spring flood and took the low row. When it went down the graves stood open and every box was empty. I have told no one. I sleep with the lamp lit now.  - A. M.
documents.canonStatus: GAME-ONLY: the register, the names and the salt custom. Hollow Men are a CANON creature (book1 ch.4).

documents.title: What the Captain Doesn't Count
documents.text:
A tally scratched on a scrap of hide, in an outrider's hand:

Khaven toll, my share, not the Company's:
  four pewter plates (the Vey woman's)
  one good knife, off a pedlar who argued
  eleven sovereigns in small coin
  a silver thimble

Captain counts the carts. Captain doesn't count me.
When the Company moves on, I don't. There's a glass ship out of Port Caelum with room for one man and no questions.
documents.canonStatus: GAME-ONLY: the outrider and his tally. Port Caelum and its glass ships are CANON (world_bible.md).

documents.title: What the Wood Repeats
documents.text:
Leaves from a daybook, the hand careful at first and less careful toward the end:

I came to Khaven to listen to the wood. My order holds that the Original Song was never lost, only scattered, and that here and there the world still hums a line of it.

Third night. While the wind blows, the wood is silent. When it drops, they begin. Not words. Names.

Ninth night. I knew one: Tamsin Ade, from the low row by the creek. Said over and over, the way a miser counts his coin.

Twelfth night. It is not the trees. Something pale stands between them, and the trees only say over what it says.

Fourteenth night. It does not sing. It counts. Every name in Khaven, and a number after each.

Fifteenth night. Tonight it said my name, and then a number.

(The rest of the page is a tally: strokes in fives, line after line, down to the torn edge.)
documents.canonStatus: CANON-EXPANDED: the Silent Pilgrims and their belief in the Original Song are CANON, and so are the Pale Things as cosmic auditors (world_bible.md); the Listener and his daybook are GAME-ONLY. Tamsin Ade is from the sexton's register (GAME-ONLY).

documents.title: Orders, the Khaven Picket
documents.text:
Oiled sheets in a leather tube, each with the Company's seal pressed into the wax: a sun on a bar of sand.

The Khaven picket, at the old north watch. Orders as given, copied fair.

Item. Khaven pays toll at its own gate as at the road: one in ten of coin, of beasts and of grain. The Company counts. The village does not.

Item (at the thaw). One Harl Emmet, of Khaven, struck a Company man at the gate over a goat taken in toll. The Company's hand is not struck twice. Hang him at the village tree, the village keeper to tie the knot and the village to watch. No salt to be laid on him. Bury him low by the creek, so that Khaven sees him walk.

Item (at the dark of the moon). A Bureau wagon comes in by the Gloom road with cargo for the Concord escort. Take the Bureau's coin at the gate, and the cargo with it, and ride it north. Ask nothing of the cargo. Count it, and send the count up the road.

Item. Any man of the picket found drinking at the Cracked Hearth pays his own score.
documents.canonStatus: GAME-ONLY: the picket, its orders and Harl Emmet. The Sandthrone are CANON (world_bible.md), and so is the Investigation Bureau's wagon (book1 ch.4).

documents.title: The Beacon Roll
documents.text:
Scratched on a slate and kept under the beacon stones, the roll of the nights Khaven lit its fire:

The fever year. Lit three nights. Oakhaven did not answer. (Hollis Grane, bearer.)
The winter the well went red. Lit one night, for the Peaks. No answer.
The night the Company came. Not lit. They had the mound by dusk.
The night the wagon came through with the children. Not lit. Tamsin says we should have. Ansel says who for.

(In another hand:) A beacon is a question. Khaven has stopped asking.
documents.canonStatus: GAME-ONLY: the beacon, its roll and the nights. The Blood-Stone Well and the Cracked Hearth are CANON (the Khaven village map); the Sandthrone and the Council's wagon are CANON (world_bible.md, book1 ch.4).

documents.title: What the Crows Wait For
documents.text:
Left in a tin under the cairn on the Heights, in Old Kestrel's hand:

The crows sit in rows on the lip and wait, and the village says they wait for the dead. They do not. I have sat with them nine nights. They wait for the pale one at the barrow to finish its sum. When it stands, they lift. When it sits, they settle. A crow knows a reckoning when it sees one.

It counts the lamps in the village. I counted with it. The village has fewer lamps than it had, and the sum comes out the same every night, which means it is counting something else as well.

If you find this, light a lamp in Khaven. Make the sum wrong.
documents.canonStatus: CANON-EXPANDED: the Pale Things as cosmic auditors are CANON (world_bible.md), and so are the Carrion Cliffs (the Khaven village map); Old Kestrel, the Reckoner and this page are GAME-ONLY.

quests.title: Break the Sandthrone Hold
quests.canonStatus: CANON-EXPANDED: Sandthrone are canon mercenaries 'often employed by the Concord but with their own agenda' (world_bible.md); their hold on Khaven and the handover are GAME-ONLY.
quests.summary: Drive the two Sandthrone outriders out of Khaven, then search their saddlebags outside the gate for proof of the handover.
quests.offer:
"Two of them. One by the well, one out on the Gloom road, and neither has paid for a drink since they came." She presses a twist of dried leaves into your hand. "For after."

"Put them down, then look in their saddlebags. They leave them on the ground outside the gate, like the road owes them. If there's anything about the little ones, it'll be in there."
quests.complete:
"Forty sovereigns," Wenna reads from the tally, flat. "Half at our gate, half 'at the toll'. There's only one toll anyone means round here: the Sandthrone road over the Peaks."

"Go and see Ansel Morrow at the Crypt-Keeper's Hovel. He sits on his step all night. He'll have seen which way they rode."

steps.text: Drive off the Sandthrone outriders holding Khaven.
Search the outriders' saddlebags outside the gate.

objectives.say: Under a rolled cloak: a child's shackle with the Bureau's mark, and a notched tally-stick with a note wound round it.

steps.text: Show Wenna what you found.

objectives.text: Show the shackle to Wenna Coyle
objectives.say: She turns the shackle over and over. "This size. They made it this size, and they put it on a child."

quests.title: What the Pale Thing Counts
quests.canonStatus: CANON-EXPANDED: the Pale Things / Pale Kings as cosmic watchers and auditors are canon (world_bible.md, series_bible.md); the watcher at Khaven's crypt is GAME-ONLY.
quests.summary: Drive off the Pale watcher that has stood at the crypt since the wagon came, then walk the north road where Ansel saw the riders go.
quests.offer:
The old man doesn't look at you. He looks past you, at the crypt. "It came the night the wagon did. Stands at my crypt door, pale as a peeled egg, and it counts. The riders. The children. Me. I've buried Khaven for forty years and never minded the dead watching. I mind that."

"Make it stop counting. Then walk the north road past the Stillwood. The riders went that way with the children across their saddles. I watched them from my step, and I did nothing."
quests.complete: "North, then. To the toll road." Ansel lowers himself onto his step. "The Sandthrone hold the pass. They'll take coin from anyone for anything. A good trade, a child, if you've no soul to speak of."

steps.text: Drive the Pale watcher from the crypt.

objectives.text: The Pale watcher at the crypt
objectives.say: It does not fall. It stops being there, the way a sound stops, and the air where it stood stays cold a long moment after.

steps.text: Follow the riders' tracks up the north road.

objectives.text: Walk the north road past the Stillwood
objectives.say: Hoofprints a fortnight old, baked hard, going north at a trot. Where the horses stopped, the scuff of small feet. Ahead, the road climbs toward the grey shoulders of the Peaks.

quests.title: The Toll Road North
quests.canonStatus: CANON-EXPANDED: the Sandthrone charge a toll in the Shattered Peaks (the draft chapter_5.md; the Sandthrone are in the world bible); the pilgrims' rest and Maddoc Vire are GAME-ONLY.
quests.summary: Take the north road up into the Shattered Peaks and find the pilgrims' rest below the Sandthrone toll gate.
quests.offer:
"There's a rest-house on the pass, below the toll gate. Pilgrims wait there for the Sandthrone to name a price. Maddoc Vire keeps it. He's kept it through three sets of masters on that gate, and he writes down everyone who goes up."

"Ask him about two children in chains. And go careful. The Peaks aren't Khaven. Things up there are hungrier."
quests.complete:
Maddoc turns his book toward you. Two lines, in a careful hand: 'Two children, small, chained at the wrist. Brought up by Sandthrone riders. Taken through the gate without toll.'

"Without toll," he says. "The Sandthrone never let so much as a goat through without toll. Somebody paid before they got here."

steps.text: Take the north road into the Shattered Peaks.

objectives.say: The air thins and cools. Above you the road switchbacks over bare rock toward a wall across the pass. Smoke rises from a hut on the flat below it.

steps.text: Find Maddoc Vire at the pilgrims' rest.

objectives.text: Maddoc Vire, keeper of the rest
objectives.say: "Two children, chained, a fortnight back?" He opens a book older than you. "Yes. I wrote them down. I write everyone down."

quests.title: Grey at the Wood's Edge
quests.summary: Thin the grey wolves hunting the Stillwood beyond the walls.
quests.offer: "Wolves in the Stillwood. Grey ones, greyer every season, as if the wood's got into them." She touches a charm of knotted bone over the gate. "They've had Col Emmet's goats, and they'll have Col next. Six of them, and I'll sleep."
quests.complete: "Six. Good." She ties another knot in the cord at her wrist. "The wood will be quieter tonight. Not quiet. Quieter."

steps.text: Cull the grey wolves in the deep Stillwood.

quests.title: Mourner's Cap
quests.summary: Gather five mourner's caps from the banks of Gloom Creek for Wenna's salves.
quests.offer: "You'll be bleeding before you're done in Khaven, and so will everyone else. I need mourner's cap for the salve: black-gilled, grows on the creek banks where the water's darkest. The old folk call it that because it likes the drowned graves. Five. And don't lick your fingers after."
quests.complete: She crushes one in her palm and the smell is like wet stone. "That'll close a cut. Here, take a pot of it for yourself. You'll want it."

steps.text: Gather mourner's cap on the banks of Gloom Creek.

quests.title: Tallow for the Dark
quests.summary: Bring Cato five lumps of tallow from the carrion boars rooting under the Carrion Cliffs.
quests.offer: "Candles. Khaven runs on candles, and I've none to sell." He spreads empty hands over his stall. "The boars under the Carrion Cliffs are fat as abbots on what falls from up there. Don't ask what falls. Five good lumps of their tallow, and there'll be light in Khaven's windows again."
quests.complete: "Rank. Perfect." He wraps the tallow in sacking. "Nobody asks what a candle smells of, so long as it burns."

steps.text: Take tallow from the carrion boars below the Carrion Cliffs.

quests.title: What the Outriders Took
quests.summary: Raid the Sandthrone outrider camp beyond the north pines and take back the goods they carried off as 'toll'.
quests.offer:
"The two in the square were the polite ones." Cato keeps his voice low. "There's a camp of them out past the north pines. Everything they 'tolled' off us is sitting in their crates: my stock, the Tabors' pewter, Old Kestrel's good wool."

"Bring back what you can carry. And if a few of them don't get up again, I won't weep."
quests.complete: Cato sorts the goods with quick, careful fingers, setting the pewter aside for the Tabors. "That isn't stock. That's Khaven's." He presses coin into your hand and won't hear a word against it.

steps.text: Raid the outrider camp and recover Khaven's goods.

quests.title: The Ones Who Came Back
quests.canonStatus: CANON creature (Hollow Men: stone-grey, whispering 'Hungry', book1 ch.4); the drowned graveyard is GAME-ONLY.
quests.summary: Lay to rest the grey dead walking out of the drowned graveyard south of Gloom Creek.
quests.offer:
"When the creek floods, it takes the low graves. Always has. We'd find a boot, a jaw, and bury it again." His hands are shaking on his stick. "This year they walked out on their own. Grey. Skin like stone. Whispering that they're hungry."

"Those are Khaven's dead, and I'm their keeper. Five of them. Put them down so they stay down."
quests.complete: "Ash. Just ash and old clothes." Ansel writes five names in his book, slowly. "I'll bury what's left. Deeper, this time."

steps.text: Lay the Hollow Men of the drowned graveyard to rest.

quests.title: The Grey Sexton
quests.canonStatus: CANON creature (a Hollow Man), GAME-ONLY character
quests.summary: Destroy the Grey Sexton, the hollowed thing that keeps the creek barrow south of Gloom Creek. It is dangerous alone.
quests.offer:
"There's one more. Old Hobb Garner, who kept the crypt before me. Buried in the creek barrow with his spade, like he asked." Ansel doesn't blink. "He's up. Bigger than he was, and digging. The others come to him."

"I can't ask you to go alone. But I'm asking."
quests.complete: Ansel takes the spade in both hands. "Hobb Garner. Forty years he kept this ground, and I'll keep him now." He leans it by his door. "Thank you. That's not a thing I say."

steps.text: Destroy the Grey Sexton at the creek barrow.

objectives.say: The spade clatters down, and the thing that held it pours out of its coat as grey dust.

quests.title: The Bound Wall Breaks
quests.summary: Hollow Men are coming down off the grey scarp north of the old bound wall. See the wall for yourself, then put them down.
quests.offer: "The old bound wall. My father's father helped set it, every stone, to keep what's in the graveyard in. Nobody said what to do when they come from the other side." Ansel looks north. "There's grey things walking on the scarp above it. Not ours. Older. Go and look at the wall, so you know what I mean, and then do what you did at the creek."
quests.complete: "Five. And the wall still standing." Ansel nods once. "That's the first good news this ground has had in a month. Keep it to yourself; good news scares them worse than the other kind."

steps.text: See the Old Bound Wall, north of the village.

objectives.text: Stand at the Old Bound Wall
objectives.say: The wall is older than the village: long stones laid without mortar, and every tenth one cut with a mark like a closed eye. Beyond it the ground rises grey to the scarp, and something up there is walking very slowly, the way the hollows walk.

steps.text: Put down the Hollow Men on the grey scarp.

quests.title: Toll Without a Captain
quests.summary: Sandthrone deserters are taking their own toll on the Corpse Road from a thicket south of it. Clear them and search what they have taken.
quests.offer: Cato Brisk counts coins into a cloth and ties it. "Outriders I can bargain with. These aren't outriders. Deserters, lying up in the blackthorn south of the Corpse Road, and they stop carts with a rope across the way and take what they like." He tucks the cloth away. "My chandler's boy came back without his cart or his boots. Go through the thicket. Whatever they've boxed up, bring word of it."
quests.complete: "Boots. Three pair, and one of them the boy's." Cato turns the ledger-book you found over in his hands. "A toll-book, with no captain's mark. They were keeping the Sandthrone's own accounts for themselves. I'll see the outriders hear of it. Let them hang each other for once."

steps.text: Clear the deserters out of the Thicket, south of the Corpse Road.
steps.say: The blackthorn is cut into a bower from the inside, with a rope slung across the road and a bell on it.

steps.text: Search the deserters' strongbox.

objectives.say: Three pairs of boots, a sack of tallow candles with the chandler's mark, and under them a toll-book in a Sandthrone hand, every cart on the Corpse Road for a month, and not one coin of it sent up the road.

quests.title: Silk on the Heights
quests.summary: Dorra Vey wants spider-silk from the scree below the Carrion Heights, for a dye she will not name.
quests.offer: Dorra Vey keeps her voice down, though there is nobody near. "The scree under the Carrion Heights, on the east side. There are spiders in it now, big as dogs, and their silk is grey and strong and takes a colour like nothing I've worked." She shows you a thread wound on her finger, the red of a hanged man's face. "Five skeins. Don't tell Wenna. She'd call it unlucky."
quests.complete: Dorra winds the skeins onto a spindle, one after another, without looking at you. "Grey as the pit. Watch." She dips an end in a pot by the hearth and it comes out the colour of fresh blood. "There. Now that's a colour for a shroud."

steps.text: Take silk from the charnel spiders on the scree under the Carrion Heights.

objectives.say: A skein of grey silk comes away from the spider's spinnerets, cold and heavier than it looks.

quests.title: What the Listener Heard
quests.summary: Old Kestrel wants to know what the Listener heard before the Hush took him. Go to the Listener's Hut, then to the Hush at night, and tell Wenna Coyle what you find.
quests.offer: Old Kestrel sits with a blanket over his knees though the day is warm. "There was a man lived west of the wood, in a hut, and he listened. To the ground, to the trees, to the dead. The Listener, they called him; he had another name once. One night he walked up to the Hush and he didn't come back." The old man's hands shake. "Go to his hut. Then go up to the Hush when it's dark, and stand still, and listen the way he did. Then tell Wenna what you heard. She'll know. I'm too old to hear it myself."
quests.complete: Old Kestrel listens with his eyes shut. When you finish he opens them. "A name. He heard a name, and he went up to answer it." He pulls the blanket higher. "Mine's not one he'd have heard. I made sure of that, years ago. Thank you. Don't go up there again."

steps.text: Go to the Listener's Hut, west of the Stillwood.

objectives.say: The hut has no roof. There is a chair in the middle of the floor facing the north wall, and on the wall, scratched a thousand times over, one word: LISTEN.

steps.text: Stand in the Hush after dark, and listen.

objectives.text: Listen in the Hush at night
objectives.say: The wood goes quiet in a way that is not silence. Under it, very low, something is saying a name over and over, patiently, like someone calling a dog that has run off. It is not your name. Not yet.

steps.text: Tell Wenna Coyle what you heard.

objectives.say: "A name. It's always a name." Wenna ties a knot in the cord at her wrist, and another. "Tell Kestrel I said he's right to be afraid, and tell him I said it kindly."

quests.title: The Mother of the Hush
quests.summary: The grey wolves of the Hush answer to one old she-wolf, bigger than any of them. Kill her at the western edge of the Hush, and the wood may go quiet.
quests.offer: "The wolves you culled. They weren't the trouble; they were the trouble's children." Wenna draws a shape in the ash of her hearth: a wolf, and a bigger one behind it. "There's a she-wolf in the Hush older than I am, grey to the eyes, and the wood's got into her all the way down. The Hush-Mother, the hunters call her, when they'll say it at all. She lies up at the far west edge of the wood. Go in the day, go alone, and come back."
quests.complete: Wenna takes the grey tuft you bring and holds it to the lamp. It does not catch. She puts it in the fire anyway and watches it until it does. "That's the last of her. The wood will breed another in time; they always do. But not in my time, and not in yours." She unties the knotted cord from her wrist and gives it to you. "Wear that. It's done its work here."

steps.text: Kill the Hush-Mother at the western edge of the Hush.

objectives.say: She goes down without a sound, and for the first time since you came to Khaven the wood is quiet all the way through.

quests.title: The Old Bones
quests.summary: The flood gave back the oldest graves too: bare bones, walking by the drowned chapel wall. Ansel wants them laid down again.
quests.offer:
Ansel turns the pages of his book back, and back, to names in a hand that isn't his. "The grey ones were the new dead. These are older. The low graves the creek took before my grandfather's time." He closes the book. "Bones, walking. Nothing on them but mud and what they were buried in. By the drowned chapel wall."

"Four of them. I don't know their names. Somebody did, once."
quests.complete: Ansel listens, then writes four lines in the book that say only: "one of the old ones, laid down again." "It's the best I can do for them," he says. "It's more than the creek did."

steps.text: Lay the drowned dead to rest by the drowned chapel wall.

quests.title: The Bearers' Road
quests.summary: Hollis Grane carried Khaven's dead down the Corpse Road when he was a bearer. He wants to know whether the two coffin stones still stand, and what is chalked on them.
quests.offer:
Hollis Grane sits as near the Cracked Hearth's fire as a man can without being in it. "I was Khaven's smith till the smithy fell. Before that I was a bearer, like my father. The wood steadings brought their dead down the Corpse Road on our shoulders, and we rested them on the coffin stones and chalked the name on the stone, so the road would know who it had carried."

"Nobody's walked it since the deserters strung their rope across it. Go and look at the two stones for me: the one under the west thicket, and the one where the road comes down to the plague pit. And mind the blackthorn south of the road. There's men in it who'll have your boots."
quests.complete:
"Grane. On both of them." Hollis turns his cup round and round on the board. "My father. I carried him down that road twenty years back and chalked him on every stone, and the rain should have had it off inside a month."

He drinks. "Somebody's kept it fresh. Wenna, I expect. She'll say not."

steps.text: Walk the Corpse Road and look at both coffin stones.

objectives.text: The coffin stone under the west thicket
objectives.say: A long flat stone at the roadside, worn hollow in the middle by a hundred years of coffins. Chalked along its edge, fresh as this morning: GRANE.

objectives.text: The coffin stone by the plague pit
objectives.say: The second stone leans where the Corpse Road runs down to the pit. The same name is chalked on it in the same square hand, and the rain has not touched it.

quests.title: Three Turns and a Tuck
quests.canonStatus: CANON creature (Hollow Men, book1 ch.4); Harl Emmet, his hanging and the salt custom are GAME-ONLY (the sexton's register, doc.khaven.low_row).
quests.summary: Tamsin Rook hanged Harl Emmet in the spring, on the Sandthrone's word. Now he walks with the hollows of the plague pit, her rope still on him. Put them down and bring her back her knot.
quests.offer:
The Gallows-Keeper is sanding the drop's trapdoor, slowly, as if it had done something to her. "Harl Emmet. Struck an outrider at the gate who was taking his goat for toll, and the Company had me hang him for it. Hanged for a goat." She blows off the dust. "It wasn't even a good goat."

"They made me bury him in the rope, and no salt, so Khaven would see him walk. Well, he's walking. Wynn Tabor's seen him at the plague pit with the grey ones, my knot still under his ear. Put them down, and bring me my knot. I'll know it. I tie a Khaven knot: three turns and a tuck."
quests.complete:
Tamsin works the knot loose with her thumbs, the way she tied it, and coils the rope over her arm. She hangs it on a nail on the gallows post. There are a great many nails.

"That's the rope off him. He's owed his salt yet, and I'll see he has it."

steps.text: Put down the hollows at the plague pit, and find the one wearing Tamsin's rope.
steps.say: One of the grey dead wore a length of tarred hemp about its neck, tied three turns and a tuck. It went down whispering 'hungry', like the rest, and you cut the rope from what was left.

steps.text: Bring the noose to Tamsin Rook at the Gallows Tree.

objectives.say: "Three turns and a tuck. That's mine." She doesn't take her eyes off it. "Give it here."

quests.title: Salt for the Hanged
quests.canonStatus: GAME-ONLY: the crossroads burials and the salt custom (the sexton's register, doc.khaven.low_row). Salt as a ward follows the Salt-Menders' salt-magic (CANON, world_bible.md).
quests.summary: Harl Emmet was owed salt, and so is every man hanged since the Company came. Get salt from Wenna Coyle, lay it on the hanged men's graves at the Gibbet Crossroads, and see that Ansel Morrow writes it in his register.
quests.offer:
"Salt on the tongue, so the dead lie quiet. Khaven's always done it, for everybody, hanged or not. The Company stopped it for the hanged." Tamsin counts on her fingers and stops at three. "Three under the gibbet at the crossroads since they came, and not one of them salted. Harl makes four, and there's nothing left of him to salt but what you swept up at the pit."

"Wenna keeps salt, the good kind, off the Rim. Ask her for a twist of it. Lay it on the three at the crossroads and say Harl's name over them; he'll hear it there as well as anywhere. Then go to Ansel and see he writes it down. If it isn't in Ansel's book, it didn't happen."
quests.complete:
"Salt." Tamsin says the word as if it were a name too. "That's four of them lying quiet, and Harl with them, after his fashion."

"I tied the knot. Ansel wrote the line. Somebody gave the word, and it wasn't either of us." She looks north, toward the Fallen Watch. "I'll think on that."

steps.text: Ask Wenna Coyle for salt.

objectives.say: "For the hanged? About time somebody asked." She fills a twist of paper from a crock behind her bench. "Rim salt. Don't tell Cato what it cost me, or he'll want to sell it."

steps.text: Lay the salt on the hanged men's graves at the Gibbet Crossroads, and say Harl Emmet's name.

objectives.text: Salt the graves at the Gibbet Crossroads
objectives.say: You lay a pinch of salt at the head of each low grave under the gibbet and say Harl Emmet's name over them, feeling a fool. The chain on the gibbet, which has been creaking, stops.

steps.text: Ask Ansel Morrow to write it in his register.

objectives.text: Have Ansel Morrow write it down
objectives.say: Ansel opens the register to the low row and finds the line: 'Harl Emmet, the gallows. No salt.' Under it, in a hand steadier than the rest, he writes: 'Salt. Late, but salt.'

quests.title: Who Gave the Word
quests.canonStatus: CANON company (Sandthrone, world_bible.md); the picket, its orders and Harl Emmet are GAME-ONLY.
quests.summary: The order to hang Harl Emmet came down on paper from the Sandthrone picket at the Fallen Watch. Break the picket and bring Tamsin Rook its order-roll.
quests.offer:
Tamsin has the rope off its nail again and is turning it in her hands. "The Company likes things on paper. The word to hang Harl came down from the picket at the Fallen Watch, sealed. Their sergeant read it out under my tree, put it back in his roll and rode home to his supper."

"I want that paper. Not for vengeance. Vengeance is a young woman's game, and it doesn't keep." She hangs the rope back on its nail. "I want it so that when the Company's gone, and it will go, there's a page somewhere that says who hanged Harl Emmet. Break the picket. The roll will be on one of them."
quests.complete:
Tamsin reads the roll by the lamp, all of it, twice. Then she rolls it up and puts it inside her coat.

"'The village keeper to tie the knot.' There it is. The Company gave the word." Her mouth goes thin. "It doesn't say who tied it. I'll have to say that myself, when the time comes. I've had the practice."

steps.text: Break the Sandthrone picket at the Fallen Watch and take its order-roll.
steps.say: The order-roll was in a leather tube at a picket outrider's belt, every sheet sealed with a sun on a bar of sand.

steps.text: Bring the order-roll to Tamsin Rook.

objectives.say: "Give it here." She weighs the tube in her hand before she opens it. "Heavier than a rope."

quests.title: Nothing That Talks
quests.summary: Nobody in Khaven will make a coffin of Stillwood timber, so the poor are buried sewn in hide. Wynn Tabor wants three hill-deer hides from the Ridge pines north-east of the walls.
quests.offer:
Wynn Tabor sits on his step with one leg stuck straight out in front of him. "The creek's given Ansel back more dead than he has boxes for, and nobody in Khaven will cut the Stillwood for coffin-boards. Grey wood talks. You don't want to be laid in something that talks."

"So the poor go down sewn in hide, the way they did in my grandfather's day. Deer's best; it keeps the shape. The deer won't come near the Stillwood now. They've gone east, up into the Ridge pines. Three hides." He slaps the straight leg. "I'd go myself, but they'd hear this knee coming from the Peaks."
quests.complete:
Wynn rolls the hides and ties them with a thong. "Ansel sews a better seam than he digs, I'll say that for him." He looks at the bundle a while.

"Nobody in Khaven goes into the ground in anything that talks this week. That's something."

steps.text: Hunt hill deer in the Ridge pines north-east of the village, and bring three hides to Wynn Tabor.

objectives.say: He runs a thumb down each hide, against the hair and back. "No holes worth the name. Good."

quests.title: The Long Acre
quests.summary: Mire boars are rooting up what the flood has left of Khaven's barley ground in the Drowned Fields, south of Gloom Creek and east of the drowned graveyard. Siv Harl wants six of them gone.
quests.offer:
Siv Harl has flour on her apron and none in her bin. "I baked for Khaven twenty years, till the oven cracked the winter the smithy fell. Nobody's mended either. Bread wants flour, and flour wants barley, and the barley ground was down the creek: the Long Acre, we called it. The children call it the Drowned Fields now, and they're not wrong."

"Every spring the creek takes a strip, and what it leaves the mire boars have, seed and root. Six of them, and I'll sow what seed I've kept and see what comes up." She looks at the sky, which is the colour it always is. "Something will. Something always does, here."
quests.complete: "Six." Siv wipes her hands on her apron, which only makes them floury. "Mattock will say it was the creek all along and the boars only finishing up. Let him. I'll sow tomorrow."

steps.text: Kill mire boars in the Drowned Fields, south of Gloom Creek and east of the drowned graveyard.

quests.title: Hush-Teeth
quests.summary: Mattock Jenn sells wolf's-tooth charms to the frightened, and the Sandthrone are the most frightened customers he has. He wants four wolf fangs, from any wolf at all.
quests.offer:
Mattock Jenn keeps the far end of the chandler's stall. There is very little on it, laid out very tidily. "The Company men are frightened of the Stillwood. Big men, good swords, and they won't stand under a grey tree after dark. Frightened men buy charms, and the charm they'll pay for is a tooth off a Hush wolf, on a thong."

"Any wolf's tooth, mind. I'll tell them it's from the Hush. They can't tell the difference, and it does them exactly as much good." He straightens a thong that is already straight. "Four fangs. Siv calls it selling lies. I call it selling sleep."
quests.complete:
Mattock threads the teeth on thongs with quick, neat fingers and hangs them at the front of the stall, where an outrider would see them first. "Hush-teeth. A crown apiece, two for the nervous."

He pays you out of the first sale before it has been made.

steps.text: Take fangs from the grey wolves of the Stillwood or the Hush, and bring four to Mattock Jenn.

objectives.say: "Good long ones." He holds one up to the lamp. "That one's from the Hush if ever I saw one. Which I haven't."

quests.title: The Name in the Well
quests.canonStatus: CANON-EXPANDED: the Blood-Stone Well is CANON (the Khaven village map), and so are the Pale Things as cosmic auditors (world_bible.md); the naming custom is GAME-ONLY.
quests.summary: Old Kestrel's true name went down the Blood-Stone Well the night he was born, as Khaven names did once. He wants to know whether the counting thing has learned to read the well. Look into it after dark, then ask Ansel Morrow what name the pale watcher called him by.
quests.offer:
Old Kestrel lowers his voice, though only the crows are listening. "Kestrel's not my name. It's what my mother called me, for I was thin and sharp in the nose. My name she whispered down the Blood-Stone Well the night I was born, as Khaven mothers did then, and nobody's said it aloud since. Not even me. That's how I made sure."

"The thing the Listener heard counts names. If it's learned to read the well, all my care's been no more use than this blanket." He grips your sleeve. "Look into the well after dark, and listen. Then ask Ansel Morrow what the pale thing at his crypt called him. Ansel's a by-name too. Don't tell him I said so."
quests.complete:
"Held." Old Kestrel lets go of the blanket he has been twisting. "Well, then. Well."

"But a thing that counts doesn't stop because the sum won't come out. It goes looking for the figures it's missing." He looks east, toward the Carrion Heights and the crows. "Come back when you're stronger. I'll have thought how to ask you."

steps.text: Look into the Blood-Stone Well after dark, and listen.

objectives.say: You lean over the well's red lip. Far down, the water is red even in the dark, and perfectly still. You listen a long while. It says nothing at all, the way a locked box says nothing.

steps.text: Ask Ansel Morrow what name the pale watcher called him.

objectives.say: "Ansel. It counted me as Ansel, every night it stood there." Something like a smile. "That's not the name my mother gave the well. Tell Kestrel the well's held."

quests.title: The Final Sum
quests.canonStatus: CANON-EXPANDED: the Pale Things / Pale Kings as cosmic auditors are CANON (world_bible.md); the Pale Reckoner and the Charnel Barrow are GAME-ONLY.
quests.summary: A pale thing far bigger than the watcher at the crypt sits at the Charnel Barrow on the Carrion Heights, adding up Khaven. Destroy the Pale Reckoner and bring Old Kestrel its slate. It is past what one blade can do alone.
quests.offer:
"The crows came down off the Carrion Heights last night, every one, and sat in rows on our roof till it was light." Old Kestrel's hands are steady for once. "Wenna says something's put them off their perch. Something bigger than a crow."

"The Charnel Barrow, up on the Heights, where Khaven carried its old bones out of the flood's reach. There's a pale thing sitting among them, bigger than the one at Ansel's crypt, with a slate on its knee, adding us up: the bones' names, the living's, and the ones it hasn't got." He lets go of the blanket. "They say it's past one blade. Take friends. Then bring me the slate. I want to see what I come to."
quests.complete:
Old Kestrel holds the slate to the lamp and reads down it with one finger, his lips moving. Wenna's name. Ansel's. Dorra's, and he stops there a long moment. Near the bottom, 'Kestrel', and after it, where the number should be, the glass is scratched and scratched again and left blank.

"It couldn't finish me." He laughs, for the first time since you have known him, and it turns into a cough. "Put it on the fire. No. Give it here. A man ought to know what he's worth, even when it's nothing anybody can count."

steps.text: Destroy the Pale Reckoner at the Charnel Barrow on the Carrion Heights, and take its slate.
steps.say: Where the Reckoner sat, a pane of pale glass lies face down among the bones, cold enough to hurt the fingers.

objectives.say: Its last blow never lands. It sets down its hand like a clerk at the end of the day, and is gone, and every crow on the Heights goes up at once.

steps.text: Bring the slate to Old Kestrel.

objectives.say: "Give it here. Gently. It's all of us on there."

quests.title: Light for the Pass
quests.canonStatus: GAME-ONLY: the candles. The Sandthrone toll in the Peaks is CANON-EXPANDED (the draft chapter_5.md); Maddoc Vire and the pilgrims' rest are GAME-ONLY.
quests.summary: Cato Brisk has made candles of the carrion-boar tallow and sold a bundle to Maddoc Vire, who keeps the pilgrims' rest on the pass below the Sandthrone toll gate. Carry it up the north road into the Shattered Peaks.
quests.offer:
Cato Brisk is wrapping candles in sacking, a dozen to a bundle. "Your tallow, these. Rank as sin, and they burn all night." He ties the twine with a merchant's knot. "There's a rest-house up the north road, on the pass below the Company's toll gate. Maddoc Vire keeps it. Pilgrims sit there in the dark for days, waiting on the Sandthrone to name a price, and Maddoc writes every one of them down. A man can't write in the dark."

"He's paid me for a bundle already, in advance, which nobody does. Take it up to him. Mind the sacking; they mark."
quests.complete:
Maddoc sets a candle in the neck of a bottle and lights it, and the pilgrims on the benches turn their faces to it the way you would to a fire. He breathes in, and his face does something complicated. "Boar."

"Well. They'll see to write by, and that's all a candle's for. Tell Cato he's paid. Tell him I'll want another bundle before the snow, and I'll pay for that one in advance as well, more fool me."

steps.text: Take the candles up the north road to Maddoc Vire at the pilgrims' rest in the Shattered Peaks.

objectives.say: "Cato's candles? Paid for and come at last." He weighs the bundle in both hands. "Heavier than I paid for. That's not like Cato."
